Mobile in brief

Where Mobile Bay begins, the port city of Mobile ranks second in Alabama by population: 187,041 in 2020 and an estimated 204,689 following an annexation in 2023. The land rises from 10 feet along downtown's Water Street to 211 feet near Mobile Regional Airport. Within a few blocks, one house may flood while another stays dry.

Historic districts are plentiful: Ashland Place, Campground, Church Street East, De Tonti Square, Leinkauf, Lower Dauphin Street, Midtown, Oakleigh Garden, Old Dauphin Way, Spring Hill and Toulminville. Houses there often date back a hundred years or longer. Expect questions from a buyer or lender about the roof, wiring, plumbing and foundation, and a repair bill can take a real bite out of a retail sale. A cash buyer who takes the house as is avoids that haggling.

Midtown took the worst of the tornado of December 25, 2012, with damage to at least 100 structures along streets such as Carlen Street, Rickarby Place, Dauphin Street, Old Shell Road and Springhill Avenue.

Who bills the tax and when

Inside city limits, billing and collection belong to the Mobile County Revenue Commission. Offices shut every Wednesday, which means any visit has to be on another weekday.

The October 1 due date is followed by delinquency when December 31 ends. An unpaid account reaches probate court in February, gets advertised in April and can be sold in May.

Totals vary with the school district. The Mobile County Public School System serves most addresses, while Chickasaw, Saraland and Satsuma operate separate systems, so check closely if you live near one of those boundaries.

Water, storms and what buyers check

One 2007 study ranked Mobile the wettest city in the lower 48, averaging 66.3 inches of rain a year. That puts steady strain on roofs, gutters and crawl spaces, with July and August the soggiest months.

Hurricanes are part of local history. Frederic came through in 1979 at Category 3. Opal (1995) and Ivan (2004) caused moderate damage. In 2005 Katrina's 11.45-foot surge put downtown and the elevated Jubilee Parkway underwater. Sally crept through in 2020 as a Category 2, with Zeta arriving a month after.

Heat and humidity matter more than cold to a local inspector, who looks at air conditioning, moisture and mold first. Cash buyers accept storm-damaged or half-repaired houses in their present state, so you need not finish the work before closing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer and recording

Deeds are recorded at the county probate office. Under Alabama Code 40-22-1 the recording privilege tax is $0.50 per $500 of value, and a sworn sale price form has to accompany the deed. Leaving the price off or misstating it risks a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax, whichever is larger. The state receives two thirds of the deed tax and the county one third.

Task at a saleWhere it happens
Pay or clear the current tax balanceUsually at closing, handled by the title company
Sign a deed matching the legal descriptionClosing table
Submit the sale price form with the deedProbate office
Assess the house in the buyer's nameRevenue Commission

How to challenge an assessment

To contest an assessed value, go to the county Board of Equalization. If you still disagree with its final decision, Alabama Code 40-3-25 allows 30 days to take the case to circuit court, with notice to the board secretary and circuit clerk plus a bond.

Prior-year taxes must be paid before they go delinquent, or the court may dismiss the case. Stopping payment while you appeal is a good way to lose.

Selling with tax due

You need not pay the balance beforehand. A title company requests the payoff from the Revenue Commission and deducts it from the proceeds at closing. Get that figure before saying yes to an offer, because it determines what you really keep.

Acting before January keeps the account out of the delinquency process. Come February the file belongs to the probate court, and clearing it costs more.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What Mobile sellers usually face

Most Mobile sellers own an older house, show storm wear and face a tax or probate question. Families in historic neighborhoods often hold a house for decades and then inherit it, and it may sit while an estate is opened. The county's 184,441 housing units in 2020 included 11.2% vacant ones, so empty houses are a visible part of this market.

Cash Home Buyers buys Mobile houses in their present condition, whether tax is due, repairs were put off or a storm left damage. Any balance owed is paid by the title company from proceeds. With no lender appraisal involved, a roof that would fail a mortgage inspection does not kill the deal.

How a sale of a storm-worn house plays out

Begin with a frank list of what is wrong, from the roof and windows to drainage and whatever the last storm left. A financed buyer needs the house to pass an appraisal and usually an insurance review, and storm damage can fail both. A sale that looked solid early on can collapse weeks later for that reason.

A cash sale runs shorter. You send an address and photos, get a written offer, choose a date and sign at the title company. Tax payoff, any older lien and the deed work are handled in that single visit, with no repairs first and no lender to wait on.

What to ask the Revenue Commission

A short call covers most of what a seller needs. Ask what is owed on the parcel today, whether any earlier year is unpaid, and whether an exemption is on file that will need to change when the house sells. Ask too what the office needs to see before it will give a payoff in writing.

Remember that the office is closed on Wednesdays. Calling early in the week leaves time to fix a problem before the title company needs the number, and a written payoff protects you if the closing slips by a few days.

If the house sits near a boundary with Chickasaw, Saraland or Satsuma, confirm which school district and taxing district apply. The answer changes the bill and sometimes surprises owners who assumed otherwise.

Keep notes of each call with the date and the name of the person you spoke with, and save the payoff letter with your closing papers.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Getting your paperwork ready

Locate three things before you phone anyone: the recorded deed, the newest tax bill and the parcel number. With an inheritance, add papers showing who holds title now. The Revenue Commission can give you the present balance, and the title company can say if a lien from an earlier year is on file.

Copy the legal description off the deed. It must match county records exactly at signing, and a mismatch often delays a closing.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends the property tax bill for a house in Mobile, Alabama?

Billing and collection fall to the Mobile County Revenue Commission, whose offices are closed Wednesdays.

When is property tax due in Mobile?

The due date is October 1 every year and delinquency begins after December 31. An unpaid bill can end up at a May tax sale.

How wet is Mobile, Alabama?

Very. A 2007 study put the yearly average at 66.3 inches, the highest of any city in the contiguous 48 states.

What is the deed tax on a Mobile house sale?

The rate is $0.50 per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, and the deed needs an attached form stating the actual sale price.

Can I sell my Mobile house if it has hurricane damage?

Yes. Cash buyers purchase hurricane-damaged houses as they are, and unpaid tax is taken from the closing proceeds.

Montgomery housing at a glance

Alabama's capital sits on the Alabama River and doubles as the county seat. Its 2020 population was 200,603. State government, Maxwell-Gunter Air Force Base, hospitals and factories keep the local economy steadier than a one-employer town, but sellers still hit familiar snags with inherited houses, rentals and older homes in need of work.

The county held 105,293 housing units in 2020, with 11.5% empty, so vacant houses are ordinary here. Of the occupied homes, 56.3% have owners inside and 43.7% have renters. A lot of sellers are consequently landlords, and their rentals may have back taxes attached.

Outside the capital the county has just two towns, Hope Hull and Pike Road. An owner in an unincorporated place like Pintlala, Snowdoun or Mount Meigs still answers to the same Revenue Commissioner as someone downtown. Most addresses fall in Montgomery Public Schools; Pike Road runs its own district.

Who bills the tax and when

Houses in the city are assessed and billed by the Montgomery County Revenue Commissioner. The due date is October 1, and delinquency follows December 31. Next come probate court in February, a newspaper notice in April and the tax sale in May.

Value notices originate with the county Board of Equalization. Watch for yours in the spring and open it promptly, because your appeal period runs from the date on the notice itself, not from the day you read it.

How to appeal your value

Your request, with supporting documents, has to reach the county inside 30 days of the date shown on the notice. There is no charge and no required form, and an informal review ahead of the Board of Equalization is available and encouraged.

Appeal detailWhat to know
Deadline30 days counted from the notice date
FeeNone
Where to send itpropertytaxappeals@mc-ala.org
Phone, real property appeals(334) 832-1327
Helpful documentsClosing statements, appraisals, comparable sales and insurance values

File every supporting document along with the appeal, and sign originals. Someone living out of state may file through a representative, who needs no law license but must submit a signed authorization form.

Once the board has ruled, Alabama Code 40-3-25 allows 30 days to go to circuit court. Prior-year taxes have to stay current while the case is pending.

Building a strong appeal file

Because the board works from paper, your file does the talking. Closing statements from nearby sales show what buyers really paid. An appraisal from a refinance or purchase offers a professional opinion. Insurance values indicate the cost of rebuilding. Photos and repair estimates explain a gap between your house and a similar one on the next street.

Put your name and the parcel number on each page, sign the originals and keep copies. Asking for the informal review first may resolve things before the board is involved, and trying costs nothing.

Heat, hail and the roof

Montgomery summers drag on, with about 86 days a year above 90 degrees and heat indexes frequently at 100 or higher. Spring storms may carry big hail, strong wind and tornadoes, and weakened tropical systems can dump heavy rain.

Inspectors therefore begin with the roof, then check drainage and the air conditioner. A big snowstorm comes about once a decade, which makes freeze damage a smaller worry than heat and storms. If your roof or cooling unit is worn out, a cash buyer will take the house with it.

Recording and closing

Deeds go to the probate judge for recording. Before one is accepted, the recording privilege tax of $0.50 per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1 must be paid, and a form giving the actual purchase price must accompany it.

Any unpaid property tax is deducted from the seller's proceeds by the title company.

  • Get a payoff figure from the Revenue Commissioner.
  • Gather the deed, closing statement and any survey.
  • Record the deed with the probate judge once you close.
  • Buyers should have the house assessed in their own name.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Landlords selling a rental

When over four in ten occupied homes are rentals, a Montgomery sale frequently includes a tenant. Check the lease for its end date and any showing rules, and let the tenant know what is coming before a stranger arrives.

Landlords are also the owners most likely to have older tax years open. Find out from the Revenue Commissioner if several years are unpaid, since each gets separate advertising and fees after delinquency. If you pay in pieces, start with the oldest year and save every receipt.

A cash buyer can often close with the tenant staying or with the house vacant. State your preference when you request an offer.

A simple timeline for a Montgomery sale

Week one is for facts. Get the payoff, confirm who holds title and decide whether tenants stay. Week two is for offers: compare the net on each, after tax and closing costs, not just the headline price. After you accept, the title company runs its search, orders the payoff in writing and prepares the settlement statement.

Closing day should hold no surprises if you read that statement ahead of time. Check the tax line, the deed details and your proceeds. Afterward the deed is recorded and the buyer assesses the house in their own name.

If you inherited the house, expect one more step. The title company will want proof of who holds title, and it may ask for papers from the estate before it schedules the closing. Start collecting those early, because a missing document is the most common cause of delay and is rarely something the buyer can fix for you.

Bring a photo ID to the closing. Keep the final settlement statement and the paid receipt for your records. If a question about the tax ever comes up later, those two pages answer it, and having them in one folder saves a search through old mail.

If a buyer's agent asks questions about the tax history, point them to the Revenue Commissioner instead of guessing. A wrong figure from you can slow the deal more than a short wait for the right one.

Selling with back taxes

Owing tax does not prevent a sale. The Revenue Commissioner quotes a payoff, the title company settles it out of your proceeds, and the remainder is yours. A payoff holds only for the date it was figured, so the closer may request a fresh one if closing moves. Try to finish before April advertising, and ideally before delinquency in January.

Anyone appealing a value while planning to sell should raise it with the closing attorney first, because the appeal rules demand current prior-year taxes.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What Montgomery sellers face

Cash Home Buyers purchases Montgomery houses in their present condition, back taxes included, with the title company paying unpaid property tax from proceeds. Because no lender is involved, no appraisal has to be passed and no repair list answered.

Whoever you plan to call, first locate the deed and the latest tax notice and ask the Revenue Commissioner if anything is owed. With an inheritance, add papers showing the current titleholder.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends Montgomery, Alabama property tax bills?

Bills come from the Montgomery County Revenue Commissioner, who also assesses houses inside the city.

When is Montgomery property tax due?

The due date is October 1, and the account is delinquent after December 31.

How long do I have to appeal my Montgomery property value?

Thirty days, counted from the date on your notice. Filing costs nothing.

What documents help a Montgomery appeal?

Closing statements, appraisals, comparable sales and insurance values are good examples. File them with the appeal itself.

Can I sell a Montgomery house that has unpaid property tax?

Yes. Proceeds at closing pay the balance. Ask the Revenue Commissioner for a payoff beforehand.

Cash Home Buyers in Alabama
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Tuscaloosa, AL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Tuscaloosa property tax?

Tuscaloosa at a glance

Tuscaloosa sits beside the Black Warrior River in west-central Alabama, roughly 60 miles southwest of Birmingham, and serves as the county seat. The 2020 count was 99,600 residents and the 2025 estimate is 114,288, which makes it the fifth most populous city in the state. The 2020 figure was a 10.1 percent rise from 2010.

Buyers often search by neighborhood, and names that come up include Alberta, Downtown, East Tuscaloosa, Hillcrest, North River, West Tuscaloosa, Central and Midtown, and the University of Alabama campus area. Houses near campus, near the retail corridor around 15th Street and McFarland Boulevard, and along the river can each appeal to a different kind of buyer. Lake Tuscaloosa is wholly within city limits, which shapes lakefront demand.

Who bills property tax

City hall does not issue the tax bill; county offices do. The Tax Assessor values the property and the Tax Collector bills and collects, both at 714 Greensboro Ave, with the collector in Room 124 and the assessor in Room 108. The collector's main line is (205) 464-8230, and the assessor's is (205) 464-8240.

Due dates and penalties

DateWhat happens
October 1Taxes are due
December 31Last day to pay without penalties or interest; a postmark of that day is accepted
January 1Taxes are delinquent and delinquent notices go out
After March 15Personal checks are no longer accepted
AprilOnline tax sale is advertised, then held in the last week of the month

These dates follow the statewide schedule. Delinquency only gets more expensive with time, so deal with an old balance before you list the house.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How the county values a city house

Values are reviewed on a four-year cycle by the appraisal staff, and they look again in between when a building permit, septic permit, recent sale or taxpayer request triggers it. A recently permitted remodel can prompt a review, so keep the permit paperwork in your sale file.

To protest a value, send a written protest to the County Board of Equalization. Alabama allows 30 days from the written notice of valuation. Call the Tax Assessor's office to learn what it needs with the protest.

Schools

Children inside the city limits attend Tuscaloosa City Schools; those outside belong to the Tuscaloosa County School System. The city system has about 10,000 students in 24 schools, including Paul W. Bryant High School, Central High School and Northridge High School. One street over the line can mean the other system, so verify the zone before telling a buyer.

Storm history and repair records

The April 27, 2011 tornado hit Tuscaloosa hard, and parts of the city were rebuilt afterward. Ask yourself when your house was built or repaired, and keep records from that period. Buyers and insurers like to see dates for roofs, siding and structural work. Tree and roof damage from later storms should be documented the same way.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

An old balance will not stop you from selling. Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff. Your title company uses that number and pays the balance from your proceeds at closing. If a bill was mailed to an old address, confirm your current mailing address with the collector's office so notices reach you.

Take along the deed, a photo ID and your newest tax statement. Where heirs share the house, every owner generally signs, so start that conversation early.

Paying and avoiding trouble

The simplest way to avoid penalties is to pay before the last day of December. A postmark of December 31 is accepted, but a payment that is mailed late or lost in the post can still leave the account delinquent, so mail early or pay in person. Personal checks stop being accepted after March 15, so a delinquent owner who wants to settle later in the spring should plan on another form of payment.

If you sell in the fall, decide in the contract who pays the bill that comes due on October 1. Many sellers pay a share and many buyers take the rest. Whatever you agree, put it in writing and tell the closing agent so the number on the settlement statement is right.

What to bring to the county offices

Come prepared and a visit takes minutes. Bring photo ID, the deed or the parcel number, and your last statement if you have one. If you are acting for a relative who died, bring the death certificate and any court papers that show your authority. The collector handles payment and payoff figures. The assessor handles values, exemptions and changes to the property record, so questions about a remodel or a new addition go to the second office.

If you cannot visit, phone the numbers above and ask what can be handled by mail or online. The county also runs its tax sale online, so the same habit of checking the county site pays off.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Timing a sale around the tax year

Listing in late summer or early fall puts the October 1 due date inside your sale window. Listing in winter means the account may already be delinquent, and a delinquent notice goes out in January. Either way, check the balance once at listing and again a week before closing, since a payment can post or a notice can change the number.

If you plan to sell in April or later with a balance still open, remember the tax sale. Parcels with unpaid tax can be advertised that month, which is a poor time to be surprised. A clean payoff in hand keeps you well clear of it.

What Tuscaloosa sellers run into

A college town with a storm history produces a few predictable problems.

  • Houses used as student or investor rentals that need turnover repairs.
  • Roof, siding and tree damage from storms, with repair records that buyers may ask to see.
  • Heirs who live out of town and need to settle a family house.
  • Back property tax that went to an old mailing address.

The University of Alabama is the largest employer, so demand follows the school calendar, and Mercedes-Benz U.S. International adds a steady base of workers who need housing. With a cash sale, a title company pays any county tax balance from the proceeds and you avoid waiting on a buyer's lender.

How a sale works step by step

Start with a payoff request from the Tax Collector and a look at your own records. Next, decide between an agent listing and a direct cash offer. After an offer is accepted, the title company searches the record for liens and unpaid tax, schedules the signing and orders payoffs. At the table you sign the deed, the county is paid from your proceeds and the remainder is yours.

Cash buyers skip the lender appraisal, which often cuts weeks from the timeline. That matters for a rental that needs turnover work or a house with storm repairs a loan appraiser might question.

Frequently asked questions

When are Tuscaloosa property taxes due?

October 1. December 31 is the last day to pay without penalties or interest, and taxes turn delinquent on January 1.

Does the City of Tuscaloosa bill property tax itself?

No. The county tax offices bill and collect it. The Tax Assessor handles valuation and the Tax Collector at 714 Greensboro Ave, Room 124, handles payment.

How many people live in Tuscaloosa?

The 2020 census counted 99,600 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 114,288.

When is the Tuscaloosa County tax sale?

The county advertises it online in April and holds it online in the last week of April.

Can I sell my Tuscaloosa house with back taxes?

Yes. A title company can get a payoff figure from the Tax Collector and pay the balance from your sale proceeds at closing.

Owe Huntsville Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Huntsville property tax?

Huntsville at a glance

Huntsville has 233,627 residents and is Alabama's biggest city. It serves as seat of Madison County, but the city boundary spills into Limestone, Morgan and Marshall counties as well. A Huntsville mailing address therefore does not guarantee which county sends your tax bill. Look up the parcel first. Madison County's collector bills only the land inside Madison County.

Aerospace and defense employment feeds local housing demand, with NASA's Marshall center and Cummings Research Park among the anchors. Families transferred for a contract or a plant job frequently need to close fast, and a seller who can pick a closing date to suit the buyer has an edge.

Homes range from Old Town houses dating to the late 1820s to the ranches and split levels that spread outward after Redstone Arsenal turned into a rocket research center. Plenty of the postwar houses are due for new roofs, wiring and plumbing. Inside a historic district, design review rules can apply, so phone the city before any exterior project or demolition.

Due dates and payment options

For the Madison County portion of Huntsville, the tax collector sends the bills and takes the payments. October 1 is the due date, and a bill is late once December 31 passes. Each bill covers a twelve-month span that begins the prior October 1.

State law does not oblige the county to mail a bill before the delinquency date. A courtesy notice goes out by October 1 and a final notice follows after January 1, yet a missing envelope is no defense. Ring 256-532-3370 or search the parcel online if yours never shows up.

Payment methodCost or limit
Card or debit2.75 percent convenience fee plus $0.30
E-check$1.50
Real property in April and MayCertified funds, cash or cards only

Walk-in service is at the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. There is also a satellite counter at 100 Plaza Blvd. in the town of Madison.

Tax rate and how the bill is built

Inside Huntsville city limits the county's posted figure is $5.80 per $100 of assessed value. Nearby posted figures include $6.95 for Madison, $6.15 for Triana and $4.05 for New Hope, Gurley and Owens Cross Roads. Unincorporated land shows $3.35 and improvements $3.65.

Appraised value is multiplied by a class percentage to get assessed value. Utilities fall at 30 percent and general property at 20 percent. Farmland, timber and a single-family home you live in are taxed at 10 percent. On the standard homestead worksheet, $48 comes off when assessed value reaches $4,000 or more.

What you owe depends on your own appraisal and exemptions, and only the parcel record shows both.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens if the tax goes unpaid?

Once December 31 passes, a $5.00 late fee attaches and interest builds at 1 percent monthly on the base tax. Probate and advertising charges pile on top.

Delinquency begins January 1 under the state schedule. Probate court receives the file in February, hears matters in March, and notices are advertised in April. The sale comes in May, and Madison County runs its yearly lien auction online.

Settling the account ahead of the auction is much cheaper than redeeming afterward. When back taxes are what is pushing you to sell, say so up front so the title company can put the exact payoff on the closing statement.

How to appeal your assessment

A written protest goes to the Madison County Board of Equalization, upstairs in the Service Center at 1918 Memorial Parkway NW. The legal basis is Code of Alabama sections 40-3-20, 40-3-24 and 40-3-25.

  • Notice of new values usually appears in March or April as a newspaper ad that runs two weeks in succession.
  • The 30-day window to protest starts with the second ad.
  • An appraiser looks at your case first; a hearing is scheduled only if the two of you still differ.
  • Going on to circuit court means filing within 30 days after the board adjourns, with the tax paid by December 31 or a bond for twice the tax posted.

Bring photos of damage, repair estimates and recent sales of similar houses close by. An appraiser can weigh those.

What happens to the tax bill when you sell?

Tax is billed to whoever owned the parcel on October 1 of the prior year, which means a buyer may get a notice addressed to you. A new owner should check that the deed is on file with the probate office in the Service Center, then register the property with the Tax Assessor's Office and claim any exemptions.

Title companies usually split the year's tax between the two sides at closing. Request the proration worksheet and hold on to the paid receipt. Where tax remains unpaid, the closer asks the collector for a payoff number and deducts it from what you receive.

Before listing, gather your last paid tax receipt, the parcel number and the deed details. If you are not sure the deed is recorded, ask the probate office to confirm. Clearing that up early keeps a buyer's title search from turning up surprises in the final days before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Ground and weather problems that surface at sale

Severe weather is the chief hazard. Spring and late fall storms bring big hail, damaging wind and tornadoes, and Huntsville lies in Dixie Alley, known for long-track twisters. Damaged roofs and siding come up quickly with buyers who need a mortgage or homeowner's insurance.

The ground is karst, with caves threading the limestone below. Sinkholes and odd drainage are possible. Cracks from settling, doors that stick or a soft patch in the yard tend to get flagged by an inspector working for a retail buyer.

A cash buyer willing to take the house as is sidesteps the haggling.

Common situations for Huntsville sellers

  • Inherited houses where several heirs share title and no one is the clear owner of record.
  • Older mill-village and Old Town houses that need major systems work.
  • Hail-damaged roofs from spring storms.
  • Job moves tied to Redstone Arsenal, Cummings Research Park or the auto plants.
  • Delinquent tax on a rental or vacant house.

A buyer who closes when you want and accepts the house in its present state helps in every case above. Cash Home Buyers writes offers on Huntsville houses and uses a local title company to pay off delinquent tax out of the proceeds. Skipping the lender appraisal, repair requests and financing contingency removes the usual points where a sale falls apart.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Huntsville property tax rate?

Inside city limits, Madison County posts $5.80 per $100 of assessed value. Parcels in the Limestone, Morgan or Marshall slices of Huntsville are billed by those counties instead, so confirm which one applies.

When is Huntsville property tax due?

The due date is October 1, and delinquency starts after December 31. A courtesy notice is mailed by October 1, though the county is not obliged to send one.

Where do I pay property tax in Huntsville?

Pay in person at the Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, or at the satellite counter, 100 Plaza Blvd. in Madison. Online and mail payments work too. The main phone line is 256-532-3370.

What is the penalty for late property tax in Huntsville?

After December 31 there is a $5.00 fee, interest of 1 percent monthly on the base tax, and probate and advertising costs. Parcels still unpaid can be offered at the May online lien sale.

Can I sell a Huntsville house that owes back taxes?

Yes. The balance is paid out of your proceeds at closing, using a payoff amount the title company gets from the collector.

Birmingham at a glance

Birmingham occupies Jones Valley in north central Alabama, set between long parallel ridges where the Appalachian foothills end. The city's 2024 population estimate is 196,357, inside a metro area of 1,192,583 people. South of downtown rise Red Mountain and then Shades Valley, home to the Over the Mountain suburbs: Mountain Brook, Vestavia Hills, Homewood and Hoover.

Two counties share the city, Jefferson and Shelby. Birmingham is the Jefferson County seat, yet a parcel on the Shelby side sends you to different county offices. Look at the bill itself to see which county issued it.

Annexation, including the absorption of Elyton in 1911, means neighborhoods date from different eras. A buyer will want the year your house went up.

Weather and house condition

Summers are hot, winters mild and rain is plentiful. The city also falls in Dixie Alley, a corridor with frequent tornadoes. Two F5 tornadoes hit the greater Birmingham area, in the northern suburbs during 1977 and the western suburbs in 1998, and an EF4 struck during the April 2011 outbreak. November and early December bring a second severe weather season.

Roofs, storm shelter access and insurance claims get raised in many Birmingham sales. If storm damage is unrepaired or a claim is still open, write into the contract who receives the claim money.

  • On a sloped lot, an inspector will check drainage and any retaining walls.
  • Save permits and receipts from roof or storm repairs; buyers request them.

Due dates and the delinquency calendar

The statewide due date is October 1, and a bill left unpaid past December 31 becomes delinquent. After that the calendar moves month by month, as laid out below. A few Alabama counties now sell tax liens instead, which changes the sequence, so follow the notice your own county mails.

DateStep in the delinquency calendar
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meeting
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

The Alabama Department of Revenue timetable lays out each step. After the parcel is turned over in February your choices shrink fast, so settle the bill or line up a sale ahead of that month if possible.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Where to record a deed

Jefferson County records deeds through its Probate Court. It has a Birmingham division in the courthouse at 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd. and a Bessemer division at 1801 3rd Avenue North. The recording FAQ gives office hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday.

  • Staff there will not run a title search or say whether liens exist.
  • Nor will they draft or change a deed. For that, hire a lawyer; the Birmingham Bar Association offers referrals.
  • Record Room copies run $1.00 per page, plats $15.00 per page, and certifying a document adds $2.00.
  • Recording fees vary by document. Payment can be by card, cash, cashier's check, money order or a local personal check shown with identification.

Order a title search well before closing. Only a title company or attorney can do it, and it turns up liens, old mortgages and tax problems while there is still time to deal with them.

Selling with taxes owed

At closing the title company subtracts any unpaid property tax from what you receive, then files the deed with the probate court. Ahead of that, ask the tax office that issued your bill for a payoff amount and pass it to the closing agent.

Has the house already worked through the delinquency calendar? Then collect every notice from the probate court or a lien buyer, since those parties may hold redemption rights. Our Alabama tax sale page covers redemption windows.

Bring these to the title company:

  1. The latest tax bill plus any delinquency notice.
  2. A written payoff from the office that sent the bill.
  3. Your mortgage payoff statement, if you have a loan.
  4. Photo identification for everyone on the deed.

We purchase Birmingham houses in their current state, whether older, needing work or behind on tax. With cash there is no listing period, no lender appraisal and no repair list after an inspection, which leaves title work as the main thing that sets your closing date.

What happens at closing

The sequence at a Birmingham closing is much the same for cash and financed buyers. Title work comes first, then payoff letters for every mortgage, tax bill or lien, then a closing statement and signatures. Once funds clear, the deed is sent to the probate court office for recording, and you receive whatever remains after the payoffs.

Delays here usually come from paperwork rather than price. A mortgage that was never released, a tax bill mailed to an old address or a deed with only one owner's signature can each hold a closing up for weeks. Gather documents the day you decide to sell, and have the title search run early so problems show up while you can still fix them. Ask the title company which items it needs from you and when, so nothing arrives at the last minute.

Did you inherit the house, or does the deed name someone who has died? Say so at the start. The probate court handles estates, and extra documents are usually needed before anyone can sign.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Picking the right county office

Because Birmingham reaches into two counties, a surprising number of owners call the wrong office first. The name printed on your tax bill tells you which county collects. Jefferson parcels are recorded through the probate court covered above, while a Shelby parcel goes through that county's own offices, so the Jefferson Record Room may not hold your deed.

Once you have the right office on the line, ask three things. What exactly is owed today, penalties included? Does that amount shift if closing runs late? Is a delinquency notice on file that a title company will find? Jot down each answer with the date, because the title company will compare them with its own search results.

Documents to pull together before you sell

A tidy file saves days. Start with the deed, then add every tax bill you still have, the mortgage statement, any homeowner insurance claim paperwork and receipts for repairs. If the house sits in the Shelby County part of the city, add anything that county sent you. Buyers and title agents rarely ask for everything, but having it on hand means you can answer a question the same day.

Also check the name on the deed against your identification. A maiden name, a missing middle initial or a former spouse still listed as an owner is easy to fix before closing and hard to fix on the morning of it. If the fix needs a new deed, the probate court office records it, and a lawyer should prepare it because the recording staff will not.

Finally, decide how you want to be paid and tell the closing agent early. Most sellers take a wire or a cashier's check, and the title company can explain what identification it needs for either.

Frequently asked questions

Which counties is Birmingham in?

Jefferson and Shelby. Birmingham is the seat of Jefferson County, so most owners deal with Jefferson County offices. Check which county sent your tax bill.

When are property taxes due in Birmingham?

October 1. They are delinquent after December 31.

Where do I record a deed in Birmingham?

At the Probate Court of Jefferson County. The Birmingham division is at 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd. and the Bessemer division is at 1801 3rd Avenue North.

Can the Jefferson County recording office tell me if I have liens?

No. Recording staff cannot perform a title search. A title company or attorney can, and the records are open to the public.

Does Birmingham have tornado risk?

Yes. The city lies in Dixie Alley, and the area has seen two F5 tornadoes and an EF4 during the April 2011 outbreak. Buyers often ask about roof age and storm repairs.
